title: Escalate an incident by its severity

blocks.text: The on-call desk turns every alert into an incident with a severity from 1 (worst) to 4. The response is cumulative: severity 4 only writes the incident log; severity 3 opens a ticket and does what severity 4 does; severity 2 posts to the incident channel and does what severity 3 does; severity 1 pages the on-call engineer and does what severity 2 does. Within one incident, the most urgent action comes first. Last week a monitor with a bad config sent severity 0, and nobody noticed because nothing happened.

`Escalation` already validates the monitor's name. Write `escalate(int severity)` in `src/main/java/practice/Escalation.java`, as one `switch` statement, so that each severity runs its actions in that order and a severity outside 1 to 4 throws `IllegalArgumentException` before any action runs. About a dozen lines in total.

cases.says: a severity-1 incident pages the on-call engineer
a severity-3 incident opens a ticket
a severity-2 incident posts to the channel, then also opens a ticket and writes the log
a severity-4 incident writes the log and does nothing else
a severity outside 1 to 4 is rejected with IllegalArgumentException and no action runs

origin.section: A Case Label Is Where Execution Enters, and It Runs On Until a break

concepts: A switch statement jumps to the matching label and runs every statement below it, through later labels, until a break, return or throw, so a missing break runs the next case and cumulative behaviour can be written by falling through.
A value that no label names, in a switch without a default, runs nothing and raises no error.
